name: Bract
story: Botany: the specialised leaf that holds and shelters a flower and is often the showy part (bougainvillea, poinsettia) - a holding that shelters and showcases its products; Br- of Braze plus -act of Adacta

name: Kedge
story: Seamanship: a small anchor thrown ahead so the crew hauls the ship forward by its own effort (kedging)

name: Keelson
story: Shipbuilding: the internal backbone bolted on top of the keel that stiffens the whole hull; sounds like a surname

name: Strake
story: Shipbuilding: one continuous line of hull planking running stem to stern

name: Burl
story: Woodworking: the rare figured growth prized as the most valuable wood

name: Carvel
story: Shipbuilding: carvel planking laid flush edge to edge for a smooth, strong hull; the caravel of the explorers

name: Colophon
story: Printing: the printer's mark and statement at the end of a book naming who made it - the maker's signature

name: Touchmark
story: Pewtering: the maker's mark each master was required to strike on his ware, taking personal responsibility for quality

name: Spelter
story: Metalworking: the zinc-copper filler alloy used in brazing (spelter brazing) - the metal that joins parts into one stronger piece; a hidden nod to Braze

name: Wootz
story: Metallurgy: the legendary crucible steel of South India behind Damascus blades, traded worldwide as the most valuable steel

name: Planish
story: Metalworking: planishing is the final hammer work that smooths and hardens sheet metal - the finishing pass

name: Faber
story: Latin: craftsman, smith; 'faber est suae quisque fortunae' - every man is the maker of his own fortune

name: Auctor
story: Latin: originator, founder and also the guarantor who vouches for what he sells; root of author and authority

name: Fecit
story: Latin 'made (it)': the signature formula on artworks and instruments ('Stradivarius fecit')

name: Factum
story: Latin: a deed, a thing done; 'factum est' - it is done

name: Facta
story: Latin 'facta, non verba' - deeds, not words: the no-sales-talk voice

name: Hexis
story: Greek: Aristotle's settled disposition; excellence as a habit - 'we are what we repeatedly do'

name: Propria
story: Latin 'propria manu' - by one's own hand, the signature formula; propria = one's own

name: Proprium
story: Latin: one's own; property; a distinguishing characteristic

name: Gilda
story: Medieval Latin gilda, the guild: craftsmen who owned their trade and its quality rules; also a woman's name

name: Crispin
story: St Crispin, patron saint of shoemakers and craftsmen; the St Crispin's Day 'band of brothers' speech - a small team, a big outcome

name: Brunel
story: Isambard Kingdom Brunel, Victorian engineer who owned whole projects end to end: railways, bridges, the great steamships

name: Dunstan
story: St Dunstan, 10th-century archbishop, goldsmith and metalworker, patron saint of goldsmiths

name: Kothar
story: Kothar-wa-Khasis, the Ugaritic god of craftsmanship ('skilled and wise') who built Baal's palace

name: Ilmari
story: Short for Ilmarinen, the Finnish eternal hammerer who forged the Sampo, the mill that produces endless wealth; a Finnish first name

name: Sampo
story: Finnish myth: the magic mill forged by Ilmarinen that grinds out flour, salt and gold forever - the ultimate value-producing product

name: Kaveh
story: Kaveh the Blacksmith (Shahnameh) raised his leather apron as a banner and it became the royal standard of Persia

name: Aldus
story: Aldus Manutius, Venetian printer who invented italic type and the pocket book - a product innovator

name: Svarog
story: Slavic smith god of fire and sky who forged the sun and taught people metalwork

name: Caxton
story: William Caxton set up England's first printing press (1476) and owned the whole product: translating, editing, printing, selling

name: Prova
story: Word: Italian/Portuguese 'proof, trial'. Acronym: Products · Responsibility · Ownership · Value · Accountability

name: Obra
story: Word: Spanish/Portuguese 'a work, a built work' (obra maestra). Acronym: Ownership · Build · Results · Accountability

name: Sova
story: Word: Serbian 'owl' (wisdom). Acronym: Ship · Own · Value · Always

name: Verso
story: Word: printing term for the left-hand page; Italian 'toward'. Acronym: Value · Execution · Responsibility · Ship · Ownership

name: Arca
story: Word: Latin strongbox, coffer where value is kept. Acronym: Accountable · Reliable · Crafted · Always shipping

name: Trova
story: Word: Italian 'finds'. Acronym: Think · Responsibility · Ownership · Value · Action

name: Brava
story: Word: Italian 'well done'. Acronym: Build · Responsibility · Accountability · Value · Always

name: Avow
story: Word: English 'to declare openly, to own up to'. Acronym: Accountability · Value · Ownership · Work

name: Zamak
story: Word: the die-cast zinc alloy whose name is itself an acronym (Zink · Aluminium · MAgnesium · Kupfer); in Croatian/Slavic 'zamak/zamek' = castle, keep

name: Alnico
story: Word: the permanent-magnet alloy named from its elements (AL · NI · CO) - it holds its pull for decades

name: Kremen
story: Serbian/Slavic 'flint', the stone that strikes fire; 'čovek od kremena' = a man of flint, a person of integrity

name: Esnaf
story: Balkan/Ottoman craft guild (from Arabic asnaf) with strict quality rules for masters

name: Kalfa
story: Balkan guild rank between apprentice (šegrt) and master (majstor): the journeyman who carries real work

name: Makar
story: Scots 'makar' = maker, the poet as craftsman; Scotland's national poet is titled the Makar

name: Kaji
story: Japanese kaji: blacksmith (鍛冶), and also rudder (舵)

name: Obraz
story: Serbian 'obraz': honour, integrity, face ('imati obraza')

name: Bakar
story: Serbian/Croatian 'copper': the metal that conducts and joins

name: Kalvis
story: Lithuanian 'smith'; Kalvelis is the celestial smith who forges the sun

name: Ricasso
story: Bladesmithing: the unsharpened flat of a blade where the smith stamps his maker's mark

name: Aurifex
story: Latin: goldsmith, literally 'gold-maker' (aurum + facere)

name: Fleuron
story: Typography: the printer's flower ornament

name: Pilcrow
story: Typography: the paragraph mark (¶) that opens a new thought

name: Argosy
story: A richly laden merchant ship; the word comes from Ragusa (Dubrovnik) - a Balkan origin for 'rich cargo'

name: Sinter
story: Process engineering: fusing powder into a dense solid part with heat and pressure, without melting - many small parts become one strong piece

name: Ducat
story: The Venetian gold ducat, Europe's most trusted coin for six centuries

name: Freehold
story: English law: the most complete ownership - you own it outright, forever

name: Heft
story: English: the felt weight and substance of a well-made thing

name: Allod
story: Medieval Latin allodium: land held in absolute ownership, owing nothing to any lord

name: Bosk
story: Archaic English: a small wood, a thicket

name: Proba
story: Latin/Serbian 'proba': proof, test, rehearsal

name: Cermet
story: Materials engineering: a ceramic-metal composite with the hardness of ceramic and the toughness of metal

name: Handsel
story: Old English/Norse handsal: the handshake that sealed a bargain; the first money a new business takes

name: Rowan
story: The rowan tree, sacred to Brigid in Celtic lore; a given name that hides 'own'

name: Hewn
story: English: shaped by hand with an axe ('hand-hewn')

name: Vested
story: English: fully owned (vested equity) - builders with skin in the game

name: Gowan
story: Scottish/Irish surname from Gaelic gobha, smith; hides 'own'

name: Exergy
story: Thermodynamics: the part of energy that can do useful work - the engineer's measure of real value

name: Carnot
story: Sadi Carnot, who defined the maximum efficiency any engine can reach

name: Pragma
story: Greek pragma: a deed, a thing done, business; root of 'pragmatic'; #pragma in C
